items.readable_text:
Content:
If [MATH: n] is any rational number, then we can expand the expression [MATH: (1+x)^n] using the generalized binomial theorem:

Content:
[MATH: (1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)x^2}{2!} + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)x^3}{3!}+\cdots.]
This series is convergent whenever [MATH: |x| < 1.]

Content:
It's important to note that the constant term in our binomial must equal [MATH: 1] for these formulas to apply.

Content:
Now, suppose that we want to find a binomial expansion of the following expression:

Content:
[MATH: \sqrt{2+4x}.]

Content:
First, let's rewrite our expression as

Content:
[MATH: (2+4x)^{1/2}.]

Content:
Notice that the constant term in this binomial is [MATH: 2,] not [MATH: 1.] So, to apply the generalized binomial theorem, we must rewrite our expression to make the constant term inside the parentheses equal to [MATH: 1.]

Content:
To do this, we first take out a factor of [MATH: 2] and apply the power of product rule:
[MATH: \eqalign{
(2+4x)^{1/2} &= (2(1+2x))^{1/2}\[5pt]
&= 2^{1/2} (1+2x)^{1/2}
}]

Content:
Then, we apply our generalized binomial formula with [MATH: n=\dfrac{1}{2}] and [MATH: 2x] instead of [MATH: x{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
2^{1/2} (1+2x)^{1/2}
&= 2^{1/2} \left[1 + {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}(2x) + \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}-1\right)}(2x)^2}{2!}+ \cdots \right]\
&= \sqrt{2} \left[1 + x + \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} 4x^2}{2}+ \cdots \right]\
&= \sqrt{2} \left[1 + x - \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \cdots \right].
}]

Content:
This series converges if [MATH: |2x|< 1,] or equivalently, [MATH: |x| < \dfrac{1}{2}.]

The generalized binomial formula states that [MATH: (1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)x^2}{2!} + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)x^3}{3!}+\cdots.]

Now, applying the generalized binomial formula with [MATH: n=-1] and [MATH: -\dfrac{1}{3}x] instead of [MATH: x,] we obtain [MATH: (6)/(3 − x)|= 2(1 − (1)/(3)x)^{− 1}; = 2[1 + (− 1)(− (1)/(3)x) + ((− 1)(− 1 − 1)(− (1)/(3)x)^{2})/(2!) + ⋯]; = 2[1 + (1)/(3)x + ((− 1)(− 2)((1)/(9))x^{2})/(2) + ⋯]; = 2[1 + (1)/(3)x + (1)/(9)x^{2} + ⋯]; = 2 + (2)/(3)x + (2)/(9)x^{2} + ⋯.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The generalized binomial formula states that [MATH: (1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)x^2}{2!} + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)x^3}{3!}+\cdots.]

Factoring [MATH: 2] out of the binomial, we rewrite the given expression as [MATH: \eqalign{ \sqrt{2}(2-x)^{-{1}/{2}} & = \sqrt{2}\left(2\left(1-\frac{1}{2}x\right)\right)^{-{1}/{2}} \[5pt] & = (2)^{{1}/{2}}(2)^{-{1}/{2}}\left(1-\frac{1}{2}x\right)^{-{1}/{2}} \[5pt] & = \left(1-\frac{1}{2}x\right)^{-{1}/{2}}. }]

Now, applying the generalized binomial formula with [MATH: n=-\dfrac12] and [MATH: -\dfrac12x] instead of [MATH: x,] we obtain

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2-x}} & = \left(1-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^{-1/2} \[5pt] & = 1+\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)+\dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}-1\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^2 }{2!}+ \cdots \[5pt] & = 1 + \dfrac{1}{4}x +\dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)x^2}{2} + \cdots \[5pt] & = 1 + \dfrac{1}{4}x + \dfrac{3}{32}x^2+ \cdots . }]

[MATH: \eqalign{
\sqrt{2}(2-x)^{-{1}/{2}} & = \sqrt{2}\left(2\left(1-\frac{1}{2}x\right)\right)^{-{1}/{2}} \[5pt]
& = (2)^{{1}/{2}}(2)^{-{1}/{2}}\left(1-\frac{1}{2}x\right)^{-{1}/{2}} \[5pt]

& = (2)^{{1}/{2}}(2)^{-{1}/{2}}\left(1-\frac{1}{2}x\right)^{-{1}/{2}} \[5pt]
& = \left(1-\frac{1}{2}x\right)^{-{1}/{2}}.
}]

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2-x}} & = \left(1-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^{-1/2} \[5pt]

& = 1+\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)+\dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}-1\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^2 }{2!}+ \cdots \[5pt]
